questions_and_answers.question_text: What are the three uses of the counter -piān?
What are the two meanings of le after an adjectival verb?
What is the difference between biéde and lìngwài?
What pattern is used with lìngwài?
How is the meaning of shénme changed from "what" to "any"?
Write the Chinese for "That wasn't what I meant."
Contrast "Wǒ yào lìngwài yìběnr" with "Wǒ yào biéde."

answers.answer_text: The first means "I want THE other one" (a certain one); the second means "I want another" (unspecified).

questions_and_answers.question_text: What does jiù shi mean here?
Write the Chinese for "Do you want anything?"
Which three adverbs are often used with biéde and lìngwài?

articles.text:
3. A: Zhèipiān wénzhāng bù hǎo ma?  Isn't this article any good?
   B: Bú shi zhèige yìsi. Wénzhāng  That wasn't what I meant. The article
      bú cuò, jiù shi chángle        is pretty good, it's just that it's
      yìdiǎnr.                       a bit long.
   B: Nǐ hái yǒu shénme biéde       Do you have any other articles?
      wénzhāng ma?

Notes on No. 3

-piān: This is a COUNTER. First, -piān is the counter for whole short pieces of writing, such as articles or essays. Second, -piān can count single sheets of paper WITH WRITING on them (compare yìzhāng zhǐ, a sheet of paper without regard to what is on it). Third, -piān(r) by itself means a LEAF of a book; that is, yìpiān(r) equals BOTH SIDES of one page.

wénzhāng: (1) "a writing, literary composition, article, essay" (counter: -piān); (2) "prose style."

Bú shi zhèige yìsi: "That wasn't what I meant," more literally, "Not that meaning (the one you just said)."

jiù shi...: Jiù here means "merely, only, just."

chángle yìdiǎnr: "a little bit TOO long." The marker le following an adjectival verb can mean either 1) NEW SITUATION, or 2) EXCESSIVE DEGREE. Sentence 3B tells you that the speaker feels the article is OVERLY long.

biéde: "other, others." Distinguish between biéde, "others in general," and lìngwài, "another" or "the other."

Use BIÉDE when you are NOT specifying "which others."
Use LÌNGWÀI + Number + Counter when you refer to a CERTAIN "other."

Nǐ hái yào kàn biéde ma?         Would you like to look at some other
                                 ones? (UNSPECIFIED OTHERS)
Nǐ hái yào kàn lìngwài yíge ma?  Would you like to see the other one,
                                 too? (A CERTAIN ONE — "THE" OTHER)

Zhèiběnr zìdiǎn bù hǎo, wǒ yào   This dictionary is no good. I want
lìngwài yìběnr.                  the other one. (A CERTAIN OTHER)
Zhèiběnr zìdiǎn bù hǎo, wǒ yào   This dictionary is no good. I want
biéde.                           another. (UNSPECIFIED)

Tāmen liǎngge rén, yíge shi wǒ   Of those two, one is my older brother,
gēge, lìngwài yíge shi wǒ        and the other is my friend. ("THE"
péngyou.                         OTHER)
Zuótian láide rén, wǒ zhǐ rènshi Of the people who came yesterday, I
Táng Huìyīng, lìngwài sānge rén  only know Táng Huìyīng. I don't know
wǒ dōu bú rènshi.                any of the other three. ("THE" OTHERS)

If you do not specify the set of things, biéde tends to mean ANY others in the whole world.

hái...biéde: The words lìngwài and biéde are often used with adverbs meaning "additionally": hái, zài, and yòu.

Tā hái zuòle biéde cài.          He made other dishes as well.

shénme: "any." The meaning of shénme is changed from "what" to "any" by the question word ma at the end of the sentence.

Nǐ yào shénme?                   What do you want?
Nǐ yào shénme ma?                Do you want anything?
